Alex M (eng-sre): Heads up — monitoring shows a sudden spike in 502/504s and increased p95 latency for hosted inference API in eu-west2 (az-a / az-b). Alerts started ~10:07 UTC. Customers are opening tickets.
Maya (support): seeing a bunch of tickets referencing request ids like req_8f3a2c and req_9b4d1e — all hitting /v1/generate -> 502 gateway. Customer says it started ~10:05 and intermittent since.
Jess (customer-success): CX flagged 3 enterprise customers, one on Dedicated falling back to hosted for promo traffic; they're getting timeouts and auth failures. They've asked for an ETA.
SRE Oncall Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457. Severity: high. Paging eng-sre and netops.
Alex M (eng-sre): Quick checks done: - edge gateway 502 spikes, upstream inference runtime returns 200, but gateway sometimes returns 502. - per-route error rate concentrated from eu-west2 -> external carrier AS12345. - short bursts of packet loss on our egress to carrier (observed via ifstats).
Ivan (netops): I pulled BGP and interface stats. Interface to carrier peer eth0 shows microbursts, RX errors on 10.24.5.2. Sample traceroute shows hop drop at provider POP: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (35.201.12.8), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.24.5.1 (10.24.5.1)  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  192.0.2.1 (192.0.2.1)  10.7 ms  10.9 ms  11.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  provider-edge-bb (198.51.100.23)  45.1 ms  46.2 ms  *
```

Ivan (netops): also saw transient BGP AS path changes for our routes at 10:06-10:08 UTC; looks like provider flapped to backup transit for a subset of prefixes.
Maya (support): any correlation with auth service? Tickets show some 401/403s alongside 502s — could be retries causing auth tokens to expire?
Alex M (eng-sre): Auth service healthy. Logs show a flurry of retries from clients after initial 502s which pushed tokens to expire for some short-lived keys (older SDKs that re-request token per call). That amplifies error surface but primary cause looks network.
Jess (customer-success): Customers want mitigation now — can we route traffic to eu-west1 fallback for host inference? They need a temporary workaround.
Ivan (netops): We can add a prefix-level policy to prefer alternate transit (carrier2) for eu-west2 egress. I'll coordinate with Carrier NOC. Potential impact: slight added latency for non-affected flows.
Carrier NOC Bot: Provider ticket TG-9987 opened with carrier. They've acknowledged microbursts on peering fabric at POP-lon-3, working on mitigation. ETA unknown.
Alex M (eng-sre): Temporary mitigation plan: 1) Add route preference to use carrier2 for problematic prefixes (Ivan) 2) Update routing policy to avoid the flapped path (Ivan) 3) Put a per-customer fallback rule in the gateway to send traffic to eu-west1 when response latency > 3s (deploy-audit required) 4) Notify customers (Jess/Maya).
Ivan (netops): Pushing route changes now — will take ~40s to propagate to our edge. Rolling back if we see adverse effects.
SRE Oncall Bot: Route update pushed by Ivan at 10:18:12 UTC.
Alex M (eng-sre): Observability — enabling detailed TCP captures on a sample edge node to confirm packet loss window.
Maya (support): Example repro steps for support playbook so we can show customers: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-v1","input":"hello"}'
# expect 200, if gateway affected you may see 502 or timeout
```
Maya (support): include the request-id header from response if present — helps correlate.
Alex M (eng-sre): Found TCP retransmit spike between 10:05:30-10:07:15 on egress. Sample tcpdump (trimmed):
```
10:06:02.123456 IP our-edge > provider: Flags [.], seq 12345, ack 67890, win 29200, length 0
10:06:02.456789 IP our-edge > provider: Flags [.] (retransmission)
```
Ivan (netops): Carrier says they saw egress queue overflow due to a misconfigured QoS on their platform that interacted poorly with a short traffic burst. They deployed a fix at 10:21 UTC and are monitoring.
Alex M (eng-sre): After the carrier fix and our route preference switch we see error rates drop to baseline over 10:22-10:30. p95 latency improving but some customers still report retries/timeouts due to previous token expiry.
Jess (customer-success): Communicated to impacted customers: provided mitigation (switch to eu-west1), temporary SDK guidance (token caching), and ETA for full resolution. Two customers accepted fallback, one asked for postmortem.
Maya (support): Closing related support tickets as "mitigated" where customers confirmed fallback worked. Keeping open a few with repro logs for post-incident analysis.
SRE Oncall Bot: Incident INC-2026-0457 status -> mitigated at 10:31 UTC.
Alex M (eng-sre): Followups: - write runbook note to detect carrier microburst patterns earlier - add automatic route fallback for edge gateways when gateway 5xx > 5% for 2m - encourage SDK team to strong-recommend token caching (reduce token churn) - invite carrier to a blameless postmortem.
Ivan (netops): I'll request a root cause writeup from carrier and share BGP snapshots + ifstats.
Jess (customer-success): I'll own customer-facing postmortem summary and share timeline.
Maya (support): tagging for CI/eval: check if any billing hits occurred due to retries — I'll open a billing follow-up ticket.
Alex M (eng-sre): Thanks everyone. Closing thread once postmortem draft exists. :thumbsup:
Carrier NOC Bot: Carrier update: monitoring shows peer stable. TG-9987 will remain open for RCA.
